steps.description: Choose Material Transfer to move stock from one branch to another. Material Receipt brings new stock in and Material Issue takes it out, so neither is what you want for a branch move.
steps.label: Stock Entry Type
steps.title: What kind of movement

steps.description: The date the goods physically moved. Stock levels change as at this date, so backdating a transfer moves the stock on that earlier day.
steps.label: Posting Date
steps.title: When it moved

steps.description: The branch the stock is leaving. Each branch is a warehouse, so this is the branch sending the goods.
steps.label: Default Source Warehouse
steps.title: Sending branch

steps.description: The branch receiving the stock. Setting both warehouses here saves picking them on every item line below.
steps.label: Default Target Warehouse
steps.title: Receiving branch

steps.description: Tick this when goods spend time in a van or courier between branches. Stock moves into a transit warehouse on dispatch and only lands at the receiving branch when they confirm arrival, so it is never counted in two places at once.
steps.label: Add to Transit
steps.title: Goods travelling between branches

steps.description: What is moving and how much. Quantities are checked against what the sending branch actually holds, so a transfer will not submit if the stock is not there.
steps.label: Items
steps.title: What is being moved

steps.description: On a transit transfer, the receiving branch does not start from scratch. They open the dispatch entry and use Create > End Transit, which fills this in and completes the move.
steps.label: Stock Entry (Outward GIT)
steps.title: Completing the transfer
